kept.reason: Its assertions check lesson close (the gh issue close call with --comment/--repo, the closed number/url, refusing non-lessons and closed issues, rejecting bad references); agent_context_lists_every_registered_command_with_its_flags_and_output_shape checks only the agent-context listing. No assertion maps, and the setups (a stubbed-gh GitHub source vs a bare run) are unrelated, so a merge would hide which behaviour failed. The overlap is shared CLI dispatch lines.

Its assertions check doctor's asks_for/hint table for four mapped commands (op, mytokens, sudo, a script), the OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN exemption and env's stderr hint; env_reads_a_service_this_host_maps_from_its_command_alone checks only the exported values of one mapped command. No assertion maps; the role's services differ (four vs one), and putting them on one role changes what env reads and exports, so the setups conflict.

Its assertions check credential-mapped exports (tool [credential] env names) of an awkward value that sh evals back, that env writes no file, the export order and the JSON role name; env_exports_a_profile_service_by_its_own_field_names checks a Profile's own field names. No assertion maps; the libraries and served values conflict (serve_values replaces the mytokens stand-in), so folding one changes what the other reads.

Its assertions check what doctor --host reports missing on the host (reasons with 'on laptop', fixes carrying --host, the stderr header naming the host and this machine); doctor_reports_a_missing_program_a_failing_check_and_a_missing_entry_each_with_its_fix checks the local reasons and fixes on another library. No assertion maps; the libraries (builder vs releaser) and the programs present conflict.

Its assertions check that doctor --project and tool install --project refuse a directory without rolesmith.toml, and the usage errors for a role or --tool with --project; doctor_help_tables_what_each_source_asks_for checks doctor's help text. No assertion maps; the only shared lines are the Machine stand-ins and CLI dispatch.

Its assertions check doctor --help's table of what each source asks for, row by row and against service_map::KNOWN; cli::help_exits_0_on_stdout checks only that the top-level --help exits 0 naming agent-context. No assertion maps; the shared lines are help rendering, and folding doctor's table into the top-level help test would hide which help failed.

kept_files.reason: Already deep: one entry point, load(root, only) -> Library | every Problem, hides reading, TOML/YAML parsing, line finding, requires closure and cycle check, external-skill fetch, tool pinning and the secret scan; callers use only load, the parsed types, valid_name, split_front_matter, Install::pinned and the limits. Its 14 commits in 90 days are features (requires, [[skill]], script install, brew stable, [service]) each adding its check to the one home of library validation, which is where they belong. Tests go through the binary; the three unit tests cover pure helpers only. Splitting the schema types from the Checker would move lines without hiding anything.
